benefits.title: Freehold ownership, open to foreign buyers
benefits.body: Emaar's guide to buying freehold property says a freehold home in Dubai is one you can fully own, outright and indefinitely, with full ownership of both property and land, the ability to resell, lease or gift it, and inheritance rights for legal heirs. The same guide lists Dubai Creek Harbour among the freehold areas open to buyers, describing it as waterfront living with vibrant dining, nightlife and luxury apartments.
benefits.sourceQuote:
In Dubai, a freehold property is one that you can fully own, outright and indefinitely. You’re not just buying the apartment, villa, or townhouse. You’re also buying a share of the land it sits on. […] Full ownership of both property and land […] Ability to resell, lease, or gift the property […] Inheritance rights for legal heirs […] Dubai Creek Harbour
 – Waterfront living with vibrant dining, nightlife, and luxury apartments

benefits.title: A route to the UAE Golden Residency (Golden Visa)
benefits.body: Emaar's investor-visa guide describes the UAE Golden Residency as a long-term residency programme and says that, for real estate investors, the current federal framework provides it to those who own one or more qualifying properties valued at a minimum of AED 2 million. Emaar also notes the Dubai Land Department's separate Taskeen investor-residence route for property owners, and advises verifying current requirements with the UAE authorities before buying or applying.
benefits.sourceQuote:
The UAE Golden Residency is a long-term residency programme available to several eligible categories, including investors. It can be granted for five or ten years depending on the type of investment and is renewable upon meeting the applicable requirements.
For real estate investors, the current federal framework provides a five-year Golden Residency for those who own one or more qualifying properties valued at a minimum of AED 2 million.

benefits.title: Developer payment plans with a reservation booking fee
benefits.body: On the Emaar online booking page for a Creek Haven apartment, checked on 9 October 2026, the reservation booking fee shown was AED 37,000, and Emaar states that your specialist confirms the payment plan for that collection before the balance falls due. Emaar's investor guide adds that phased payment plans on off-plan homes can spread payments across the development period.
benefits.sourceQuote: You will be charged AED 37,000 now (the reservation booking fee). Your specialist confirms the payment plan for this collection before the balance falls due.

benefits.title: Escrow protection on off-plan payments
benefits.body: Emaar says that for off-plan purchases, funds are held in escrow accounts managed by the Dubai Land Department, a mechanism that protects buyers by ensuring developers meet their contractual obligations before accessing the money. Emaar's own finance fact sheet likewise directs buyers to remit instalments directly to their project's assigned escrow account.
benefits.sourceQuote: For off-plan property purchases, funds are held in escrow accounts managed by the DLD. This mechanism protects buyers' investments by ensuring developers meet their contractual obligations before accessing the funds.

benefits.title: Minutes from the airport and Downtown, with a metro station planned for 2029
benefits.body: Emaar puts Downtown Dubai and Burj Khalifa at a 15-minute drive and Dubai International Airport at a 10-minute drive from Dubai Creek Harbour. Emaar also says the upcoming Blue Line Metro Station (2029) will provide seamless, eco-friendly transport access across Dubai.
benefits.sourceQuote: Downtown Dubai, Burj Khalifa: 15-minute drive […] Dubai International Airport: 10-minute drive […] The upcoming Blue Line Metro Station (2029) will provide seamless, eco-friendly transport access across Dubai.

benefits.title: Beach, parks, marina and a wildlife sanctuary on the doorstep
benefits.body: Emaar describes a community with the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary at its heart, Central Park as a green retreat with an amphitheatre, dog park and play areas, and Creek Marina and the Harbour Promenade for waterfront strolls, dining and views. Emaar also points to Creek Beach, Creekside Park and the Creek Play promenade.
benefits.sourceQuote: Dubai Creek Harbour seamlessly blends urban energy with natural beauty. At its heart is the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary, a haven for birdwatchers and home to thousands of flamingos. Central Park offers a vibrant green retreat with an amphitheatre, dog park, and play areas for all ages. For waterfront experiences, Creek Marina and the Harbour Promenade provide scenic strolls, gourmet dining, and panoramic views. Adventure seekers can explore the Creek Play promenade or the sea-themed Creek Harbour Playground by MONSTRUM. The Viewing Point, extending 70 metres over the creek, offers breathtaking cityscapes. Whether cycling along Urban Beach, relaxing on Creek Beach, or strolling through Creekside Park, Dubai Creek Harbour is where nature and adventure thrive.

benefits.title: A registered rental and resale market
benefits.body: Dubai Land Department records for the 12 months to 30 September 2026 show 3,963 new tenancy contracts and 2,465 renewals registered for apartments in Dubai Creek Harbour, with a median rent of AED 96,000 across 2,611 one-bedroom contracts. The same records show 987 ready-apartment sales registered in that window; these are registered contracts and sales, not valuations or forecasts.
benefits.sourceQuote: Dubai Land Department registration records, 12 months to 30 September 2026; snapshot taken 9 October 2026; apartments and market sales only.

benefits.title: No annual property tax
benefits.body: Emaar's guide to buying freehold property says Dubai has no annual property tax, and that investors from Europe, India, China, Russia and the GCC have taken advantage of Dubai's zero property tax. Emaar still reminds buyers to budget beyond the purchase price for Dubai Land Department fees (4%), trustee fees and service charges.
benefits.sourceQuote: With no annual property tax […] Investors from Europe, India, China, Russia, and the GCC have all taken advantage of Dubai’s zero property tax […] Beyond the purchase price, include Dubai Land Department (DLD) fees (4%), trustee fees, and service charges.
